subject.title: fix(skills): enforce byte-level cap on skill package downloads

question: Should OpenClaw cap only registry package archives, or also cap metadata-declared dependency downloads, and what compatibility limit should each surface use?
rationale: The branch combines two distinct installation surfaces with a new source-classification policy; selecting the permanent security boundary and shipped limit requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Split the boundaries
options.body: Cap ClawHub package archives in the registry client and separately design a provenance-based dependency-installer limit with upgrade proof.

options.title: Narrow to registry downloads
options.body: Remove the metadata-installer policy and implement only the compromised-registry package protection described by the PR.

options.title: Accept partial hardening
options.body: Merge this as defense in depth while explicitly accepting that ClawHub package and workspace-source downloads remain outside the limit.

recommendation.title: Split the boundaries
recommendation.body: Cap ClawHub package archives in the registry client and separately design a provenance-based dependency-installer limit with upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior work owns the adjacent resolved ClawHub install flow that must be included in this boundary decision.
